summary: An excerpt from Book 11, part 39, of a novel (Kate Douglas Wiggin's Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm style narrative) in which Rebecca is scolded by her aunt Miranda for wearing her pink dress and carrying a parasol to a school exhibition without permission, and for leaving the house careless: the screen out, a handkerchief dropped, lunch uncleared, and the side door unlocked. Rebecca admits the parasol was silly and explains she wanted to match the pink dress for a dialogue she performed with Emma Jane about a city girl and a country girl. Miranda calls her conduct crafty and underhanded, and Rebecca, in tears, explains she was late and feared a black mark before the minister's wife, the doctor's wife and the school committee.
one_line: Rebecca is reprimanded by aunt Miranda for wearing her pink dress and parasol to school and for leaving the house carelessly unlocked.
key_facts: Rebecca did not ask Miranda for permission to wear the pink dress and parasol, and she says she intended to ask at noontime but Miranda was not at home.
Rebecca says she was not certain Miranda would refuse, but thought it was worth risking because it was almost a real exhibition at school.
Miranda scornfully asks whether Rebecca was exhibiting her parasol.
Rebecca confesses the parasol was silly but says it was the only time in her life she had anything to match it, and it looked beautiful with the pink dress.
Rebecca and Emma Jane spoke a dialogue about a city girl and a country girl at the school exhibition.
Rebecca says she has not hurt her dress a mite.
Miranda calls the craftiness and underhandedness of Rebecca's actions the worst part of her conduct.
Miranda says Rebecca dropped her handkerchief on the way up the front stairs and so did not hide her tracks.
Miranda says Rebecca left the screen out of her bedroom window, letting flies into the house.
Miranda says Rebecca never cleared away her lunch or put away a dish.
Miranda says Rebecca left the side door unlocked from half past twelve to three o'clock.
Rebecca says she was trimming the schoolroom, got belated, and ran all the way home, and had time to eat only a mouthful.
Rebecca fears she would get her first black mark on a Friday afternoon in front of the minister's wife, the doctor's wife and the school committee if she was late.
Miranda quotes the proverb that an ounce of good behavior is worth a pound of repentance.
